answer: Inter-arrival jitter fingerprinting. Each identity must submit work requests whose inter-arrival gaps follow a heavy-tailed distribution seeded at enrolment; a monitor scores the short-window autocorrelation of those gaps. Accounts created in one burst share a ripple pattern no organic user reproduces, and the score decays only as a slow vine of consistent timing accrues. An attacker must run each identity through a separate throttled scheduler with randomized delays for weeks before its score reaches the acceptance zenith, multiplying per-identity infrastructure and wall-clock cost.
